questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always wanted to go to New Zealand and thought going on exchange there would be a great way of experiencing the country. I was drawn to University of Otago specifically because it's on the South Islands and close to a lot of beautiful nature and experiences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a really good time at Otago! I got to see a lot of New Zealand and experience kiwi culture.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, you receive a lot of information by email prior to your arrival. During orientation week, there's also a few different information sessions that'll provide you with all the information you need.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very easy! I stayed with Uniflats, which is the most common option for exchange students. Uniflats are small houses that you share with 4-5 other students, including one local 'kiwi host'. 

You're guaranteed a spot in Uniflats if you apply before their deadline, which makes finding accommodation stress-free.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My flat was basically on campus, but some of them are a bit further away. All Uniflats are in walking distance from campus though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed staying with Uniflats. It's a great way of meeting people, and they also host different events throughout the semester. 

The only negative is the quality of the housing (which is generally bad in NZ). The flats can get pretty cold during winter, especially in the bigger rooms. My room was pretty small and easy to heat up, so I didn't have any issues - but some of my flatmates did.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to apply for special permission for all of my courses, and initially found the procedure a bit confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You get a notification in the student portal once course selection is open. You then go through a few different steps to select your courses. Once you've selected your courses you send them in for approval. 

It's possible to change courses after the semester has started, so don't stress too much about it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There's a guide on their website, but you can also contact the university by email if more assistance is needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the courses I applied for. Most of the courses have unlimited capacity, so you're almost guaranteed a spot as long as you meet the prerequisites.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Read the guides on their website thoroughly before choosing courses. 

Also, check out the schedule of the courses before choosing them. You can plan your week so that you don't have courses on Fridays for example, if you want to be able to go on long weekend trips.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my classes. All of my professors were also super nice and accommodating

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was pleasantly surprised with the level of the courses. I took only master's courses, and they were all both interesting and challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching of the public health classes were pretty similar to what we have at home. I mostly had 3-hour lectures with discussion throughout the sessions. 

The most different thing was the assessment. Instead of exams, I had assignments which all counted towards my final grade. (Other study fields have exams, but they usually only count for some of the grade)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PUBH712: Foundations of Hauora Māori
PUBH733: Environment and Health
PUBH741: Hauora Māori- Policy Practice and Research
PUBH743: Health Promotion Programme Planning and Evaluation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed all of my classes and can recommend all of them to public health students.

I would recommend taking some sort of class on Māori culture. A lot of my friends took the Māori performance class, which looked like a lot of fun!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food was a bit more expensive than expected, and is pretty comparable to Danish prices. 

Coffee was really cheap, and would usually cost around 25 kr. Local public transportation was also pretty cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University has lots of different clubs and societies, and there's also a gym that's free to use. The student association (OUSA) offer a range of different recreational activities you can sign up for in the beginning of the year.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join any clubs, but I did sign up for a pottery class through OUSA. I can highly recommend the pottery class, as it was lots of fun and a great way to unwind a bit during the week. The teacher and the other students were all super nice, and it was a really good experience. You also get to take home whatever you make, which is a great little souvenir from your exchange!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I recommend going on trips and hike. New Zealand has a lot of beautiful nature, so you should definitely take advantage of it! There's a lot of beautiful places near Dunedin, but I also really enjoyed the West coast of the South Island, mt Cook and Abel Tasman. It's also pretty fun to go to a rugby game - and Thursday night karaoke is a MUST!

If you have the time and money, I would definitely recommend going to one of the pacific islands! I went to Cook Islands during the easter break, and I had the best time! It was such a unique experience and one of my favourite parts of my exchange trip

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I don't recall any major cultural differences

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I only had classes with local students, which made it pretty easy to make local friends. Another great way of meeting local people is to join a club or recreational activity.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't experience any major cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of the kiwis! I also really enjoyed learning about Māori culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Explore New Zealand's beautiful nature. 2) Plan your studies so you have time to go on weekend trips. 3) Go to the social events in the beginning of the semester. It's a good way to meet new people and where most people make friends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything that comes to mind!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring New Zealand, making new friends, learning about different cultures

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At times, I felt really stressed about not having enough time to see all the things I wanted in New Zealand. It took some time to accept that New Zealand is too big to fully explore during the semester while also having school to attend to

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I think Otago is a really good place to go for exchange, as the University does a lot to accommodate for their international students. Everyone lives close to campus, and there is a pretty good student life! New Zealand is also such a beautiful (and safe) country to explore.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
